issues.failure_explanation: In approximating F_N^#[x](t) = \sum_{\ell=1}^N \langle x, \underline{x}^{(\ell)} \rangle_X \underline{y}^{(\ell)}(t) by \tilde{F}_n[x](t) = \sum_{\ell=1}^N A_\ell(x) B_\ell(t), each summand is a product of an approximated functional A_\ell and an approximated function B_\ell. The error of approximating a product ab by A B is bounded by |a - A| ||b|| + |A| ||b - B|| (a sum of first-order errors), not |a - A| ||b - B||. The bound \|F_N^#[x] - \tilde{F}_n[x]\|_Y \le N q(N) r(N) mistakenly multiplies the two approximation errors without including the first-order cross terms.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the triangle inequality to bound the difference of products: \|\langle x, \underline{x}^{(\ell)}\rangle_X \underline{y}^{(\ell)} - A_\ell(x) B_\ell\|_Y \le |\langle x, \underline{x}^{(\ell)}\rangle_X| r(N) + \|\underline{y}^{(\ell)}\|_Y q(N) + q(N) r(N). Summing over \ell using Cauchy-Schwarz yields a bound of order O(\sqrt{N} r(N) + N q(N)), and propagate this corrected bound to Theorem 4.3.
issues.overall_effect: The error bound in (4.7) and the resulting convergence rate in Theorem 4.3 are invalid as stated. The discussion in (4.8)-(4.9) of the error rate N q(N) r(N) = O(N^{-1-p/2}) relies on this invalid product bound.
issues.title: Incorrect product-of-errors bound in neural linear operator approximation
issues.why_classification: The standard product error estimate replaces N q(N) r(N) with O(\sqrt{N} r(N) + N q(N)) without changing the overall proof architecture, but weakens the convergence rate and requires p > 1 in the scaling N_j ~ N^p to achieve convergence to 0.

issues.failure_explanation: Mollification does not converge uniformly to the identity on any ball in L^2: for any fixed \xi > 0 and any r > 0, \sup_{x \in B_r(x^*)} \|x - x_\xi\|_{L^2} \ge r because high-frequency components are smoothed toward zero. Therefore, Fréchet differentiability / Lipschitz continuity of F cannot establish \|F[x] - F[x_\xi]\|_{L^2} < \epsilon/2 uniformly on B_r(x^*), and the claim in the subsequent remark that \|x - x_\xi\|_{L^2} = O(\xi^2) holds on an L^2-neighborhood is false (that rate requires H^2 regularity). Furthermore, since x \mapsto F_n[x_\xi] depends on x only through finitely many scalar evaluations \langle \phi_\xi(s_j - \cdot), x\rangle_{L^2}, it cannot approximate an operator with infinite-dimensional range uniformly on any L^2 ball.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict the domain of approximation to a set that is compactly embedded in C(\bar{\Omega}_X) (such as a bounded subset of a Sobolev space H^s with s > m/2), abandoning the claim of uniform approximation on L^2-neighborhoods.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 6.3 is false. Consequently, the uniform error bound \rho_{n\xi} in (6.2) cannot be guaranteed, and the regularization parameter choice and convergence rate O(\sqrt{\delta} + \xi) derived for the c-example in Example 6.4 and the subsequent remark are unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid claim of locally uniform operator approximation on L^2 balls via mollification
issues.why_classification: Theorem 6.3 is the central result of Section 6. Uniform approximation on an L^2-ball fails fundamentally due to the infinite dimensionality of L^2 and the finite sensor architecture of neural operators; resolving it requires abandoning the advertised L^2 regime in favor of smoother Sobolev spaces.
